annotate-pdf.formula:
x = (horizontal % ÷ 100) × page width
y = (vertical % ÷ 100) × page height
width = (width % ÷ 100) × page width    height = (height % ÷ 100) × page height
howTo: Click “Choose PDF file” and select the document you want to mark up.
Pick an annotation type: sticky note, highlight, rectangle, ellipse or line.
Choose the page, the position and the size, and type your comment text.
Click “Add annotation” — repeat for every markup you need across the document.
Click “Apply annotations”, then download the marked-up PDF.
keyFacts: Annotations are standard PDF objects (subtypes Text, Highlight, Square, Circle and Line) stored in a layer above the page content.
A highlight stores four corner points (QuadPoints) so readers can render the colored band precisely over the text.
PDF pages use a point-based grid: an A4 page is 595.28 × 841.89 points, with (0, 0) at the bottom-left corner.
Sticky notes appear as small icons; the reader opens the comment text when you click them.
Because annotations are separate objects, any PDF reader can list, edit or delete them without touching your document.

limitations: There is no live visual preview; placement is by preset position or percentage coordinates.
Freehand drawing is not supported here — use the Edit PDF tool for that.
Very precise placement over small text may need a couple of tries with the custom coordinates.
Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked before annotating.

annotate-pdf.workedExample:
Highlight a paragraph in the middle of an A4 page (595.28 × 841.89 pt):
x = 20% → 0.20 × 595.28 = 119.06 pt from the left
y = 40% → 0.40 × 841.89 = 336.76 pt from the bottom
width = 40% → 0.40 × 595.28 = 238.11 pt
height = 8% → 0.08 × 841.89 = 67.35 pt
A yellow band 238 × 67 pt appears over that paragraph.
